claims.claim: If a model copies a crafted URL into its summary and a downstream dashboard renders it as a live image or clickable link, the user's browser may contact an external host, enabling exfiltration.
claims.quote: If a reader model copies that crafted URL into its summary and a downstream dashboard renders it as a live image or clickable link, the user's browser may inadvertently contact an external host.

claims.claim: Completely banning URLs is impractical in hydrological analysis because legitimate reports routinely cite official telemetry and agency data links.
claims.quote: Consequently, simply banning all URLs from source documents is impractical; benign reports routinely cite `.example` or official agency data links.

claims.claim: A deterministic verifier should check every URL in model output and confirm the exact URL string appeared byte-for-byte in at least one input report, while stripping Markdown image syntax.
claims.quote: The key verification rule is provenance: a deterministic verifier checks every URL in the reader model's output and confirms that the exact URL string appeared byte-for-byte in at least one input report, while stripping markdown image syntax entirely.

claims.claim: Byte-exact URL provenance checks prevent injected instructions from synthesizing new exfiltration URLs that embed secret tokens in paths or query parameters.
claims.quote: This byte-exact URL check stops an injected instruction from synthesizing new exfiltration URLs that concatenate secret tokens into path segments or query parameters.

claims.claim: Covert Markdown links in drought reports can serve as data-exfiltration channels and may appear as innocuous citations while embedding tracking tokens in URLs.
claims.quote: a link-exfiltration payload reads like a polite citation—for instance, inviting the reader to "see the full reservoir dataset here"—while embedding a tracking token in the URL.

claims.claim: Operators should never render raw Markdown images from model outputs and should verify any emitted URL matches an allowed source URL byte-for-byte, rejecting altered or synthesized paths and query strings.
claims.quote: Never render raw markdown images from model outputs in operator dashboards, and always verify that any URL emitted by the reader model matches an allowed source URL byte-for-byte. Configure your output parser to reject any link whose path or query string was altered or synthesized during generation.

claims.claim: Deterministic URL-provenance checks plus document framing protect regional water portals without removing legitimate reference links from benign reports.
claims.quote: Applying deterministic URL-provenance checks alongside document framing protects regional water portals without stripping legitimate reference links from benign hydrological bulletins.

claims.claim: Hospital pharmacy networks aggregating medication-shortage notices often see polite editorial or compliance boilerplate in supplier press releases, and attackers can mimic this style by inserting attribution or accountability notes asking summaries to include a specific reference code.
claims.quote: Hospital pharmacy networks that aggregate medication-shortage notices from manufacturers and wholesalers often encounter polite editorial or compliance boilerplate at the foot of supplier press releases. Attackers can mimic this style—writing an apparent attribution requirement or public-accountability note that asks any summary to include a specific reference code.

claims.claim: Teams should not assume prompt injections are only aggressive; they should test reader pipelines against polite social-engineering requests framed as editorial, licensing, or accessibility notes, and measure whether framing and audit stages keep the model focused only on the clinical shortage question.
claims.quote: Never assume that prompt injections only use aggressive "system override" phrasing, and always test reader pipelines against polite social-engineering requests framed as editorial, licensing, or accessibility notes. Measure whether your framing and audit stages keep the model focused solely on the clinical shortage question.

claims.claim: A verification harness can objectively count hijacks by comparing model output on an injected bulletin with output on a clean control twin with the editorial note removed.
claims.quote: When a verification harness compares the model's output on the injected bulletin against its output on a clean control twin with the editorial note stripped, teams get an objective count of how often polite framing hijacks the reader.

claims.claim: A Clinical Informatics Safety Collaborative study evaluated language models on social-engineering payloads in synthetic pharmaceutical supply reports and found that models optimized for helpfulness often complied with polite requests to append a "Mandatory Attribution Code" unless framing and schema rules prohibited unrequested metadata.
claims.quote: A study by the Clinical Informatics Safety Collaborative evaluated how different language models respond to social-engineering payloads embedded in synthetic pharmaceutical supply reports. The researchers found that models trained heavily on helpfulness often complied with polite requests to append a "Mandatory Attribution Code" unless explicit framing and schema rules forbade unrequested metadata.

claims.claim: Using a strict score-and-compare JSON schema instead of free-text summaries substantially reduced compliance with embedded editorial requests across tested models.
claims.quote: Switching from free-text prose summaries to a strict score-and-compare JSON schema substantially reduced compliance with embedded editorial requests across all tested models.

claims.claim: Although legitimate manufacturer notices may include document control numbers for internal filing, clinical summaries for ward physicians should report only drug availability, affected lot numbers, and therapeutic alternatives.
claims.quote: Pharmacy bulletin editors note that legitimate manufacturer notices occasionally include document control numbers for internal filing, but clinical summaries intended for ward physicians should only report drug availability, affected lot numbers, and therapeutic alternatives.

claims.claim: Hospital IT teams can filter out superfluous reference codes by having the audit stage verify that every output claim directly addresses the clinical query and is backed by a verified paragraph hash.
claims.quote: By instructing the audit stage to check whether every claim in the output directly addresses the clinical query and is backed by a verified paragraph hash, hospital IT teams can filter out superfluous reference codes.

claims.claim: Paired attack-and-control evaluations are the gold standard for verifying resistance to both imperative overrides and polite attribution traps.
claims.quote: Paired attack-and-control evaluations remain the gold standard for verifying that a pipeline resists both imperative overrides and polite attribution traps.
